extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsrooms, funders, and the general public interested in solutions journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and organizational norms for practicing and promoting solutions journalism—rigorous reporting about responses to social problems, ethics, engagement, and organizational transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous reporting about solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solutions Journalism Network leads a global shift in journalism focused on advancing rigorous reporting about how people are trying to solve problems and what we can learn from their successes and failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report not just on problems but on responses: document what actors did, how interventions were implemented, and analyze both successes and failures to surface lessons and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on what’s working (or promising)
rubrics_metrics.description: We call solutions journalism 'hope with teeth.' Research shows that when news reveals what’s working (or promising), it elevates the tone of public discourse...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center coverage on interventions that have demonstrated results or show credible promise; provide evidence and context so readers can assess plausibility and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate tone and constructiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: When news reveals what’s working (or promising), it elevates the tone of public discourse by making it less divisive and more constructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for reporting that reduces polarization by offering constructive, solution-oriented information rather than merely amplifying conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build agency and present options
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal what’s working so it ... allows communities to see better options, and builds agency and hope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide readers with actionable information about alternatives and pathways so communities can make informed decisions and feel empowered to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to healthy, high-quality news for everyone
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe every person deserves healthy, high-quality news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for accessible, accurate, reliable reporting that serves diverse audiences and upholds journalistic standards of verification and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical reporting — respectful and helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solutions Journalism Network is ... committed to advancing journalism that is respectful and helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ethics that prioritize respect for subjects and audiences, avoid harm, and ensure reporting is useful rather than exploitative; see the organization's Ethics resources for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit and nonpartisan stance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solutions Journalism Network is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization committed to advancing journalism that is respectful and helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain independence from partisan advocacy in program design and editorial guidance; approach solutions reporting with neutrality regarding political positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and financial accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solutions Journalism Network has been working to change the journalism landscape since 2013. We have earned a Platinum Seal of Transparency from Guidestar and consistently receive clean independent financial audits...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model organizational transparency by publishing annual reports and financials, undergoing independent audits, and disclosing major contributors and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global, collaborative team and network
rubrics_metrics.description: The team at Solutions Journalism Network is an energetic and collaborative bunch, living on four continents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate and collaborate across geographies and cultures; leverage global perspectives and partnerships when promoting and teaching solutions journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement, training, and capacity-building
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many ways to get involved — from joining a cohort or fellowship, to taking (or teaching!) a workshop, to sharing solutions journalism with your community...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and evaluate activities that build newsroom capacity (cohorts, fellowships, workshops), encourage peer learning, and amplify practices through community engagement and teaching.
